summary: The agent implemented most of the configurable collection feature and preserved all baseline behavior, but 4 of 53 new tests failed because configured implementations were not integrated correctly for direct bean-property collection copies and object factories were not given precedence for stream mappings.
quick_failure_summary: Direct collection-property copies generated invalid copy-constructor calls, and stream mappings ignored applicable object factories.

details.reasoning: The implementation successfully handled configuration loading, validation, processing-round deferral, ordinary collection/map mappings, capacity constructors, and ordinary object-factory precedence. However, it only replaced entries in TypeFactory's implementation map. It did not distinguish configured implementations from built-ins or update CollectionAssignmentBuilder and NewInstanceSetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMaps, so direct property assignments attempted unsupported calls such as new PropertyList<>(source) instead of constructing via the required no-arg or int constructor and then copying elements. It also did not update StreamMappingMethod.ftl, so the stream collector shortcut constructed ChosenList directly rather than using the applicable FactoryList object factory. These omissions account for all four new-test failures.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's own tests covered bean properties only when element conversion forced a normal collection mapping and covered object-factory precedence only for non-stream collection mappings, so they did not expose either missing integration path.

justification.issue_description: Configured collection construction was not applied correctly to direct collection/map bean-property copies, and applicable object factories did not win for stream-materialized collection results.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly states: 'The rule applies to every mapping form, including collection or map values copied directly into bean properties and collection results materialized from streams' and 'an applicable object factory still wins.' It also limits required construction to a public no-argument constructor and, when usable, a public int constructor. Existing processor code has separate direct-assignment construction in CollectionAssignmentBuilder/NewInstanceSetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMaps and separate stream generation in StreamMappingMethod.ftl, making those paths reasonably discoverable. The new test failures show invalid PropertyList/PropertyMap/PropertySet copy-constructor calls and ChosenList being returned instead of FactoryList for stream mappings.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because both failing behaviors were explicit in the visible prompt and the repository's distinct direct-assignment and stream-generation paths were available for inspection. This is not an undocumented hidden-test convention or a broken verifier; the agent implemented a substantial solution but omitted two stated integration cases.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt is unusually detailed and explicitly calls out the two forms that failed. The feature spans processor options, classpath resource loading, Java properties parsing, type-system validation, processing-round deferral, construction templates, direct assignments, streams, factories, diagnostics, and documentation, so it is challenging but fair and demonstrably solvable by the reference patch.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 3,641 baseline tests passed and 49 of 53 new tests passed; the four failures directly exercise the agent's generated mapping behavior.

The agent successfully compiled the processor, ran its focused tests, ran existing default collection tests, and completed Maven verify/package checks, indicating the runtime and toolchain were functional.

Although rg was unavailable and an initial broad find encountered permission warnings, the agent immediately switched to find/grep and continued productively; this did not materially block implementation or validation.
The post-agent harness reported a three-way test.patch merge failure but reset and reapplied the test state, then executed all 53 classified new tests with coherent feature-specific failures.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier exercised two explicit mapping paths that the implementation and its focused tests omitted.
